# PEN-3916 — vendor this adapter in-tree and retire `ARG OPENCODE_K8S_REF`

Brings `kkroo/paperclip-adapter-opencode-k8s` at `133f4c1a65085a6c141aab5aa8818afe51e2689c`
into the repository as ordinary reviewable source, mirroring what BLO-17980 did
for the `claude_k8s` sibling on 2026-08-06. The Dockerfile `vendor` stage now
`COPY`s this directory instead of cloning the fork, and `ARG OPENCODE_K8S_REF`
is gone.

See [PROVENANCE.md](../PROVENANCE.md) for the origin table, the single-snapshot
composition (`rev-list --count <pin>..master` = 0, so unlike the claude
vendoring there was nothing to compose), the licence caveat, and the
upstream-velocity measurement that decided it.

The main deviation from upstream at vendor time (the PEN-3732 PATH fix) is
recorded separately in
[pen-3732.md](./pen-3732.md).

## What this entry exists to record about the tree

- 44 files, the upstream tree in full. **No deliberate exclusions** — this
  repository commits no `coverage/` and no `.DS_Store`, so unlike the claude
  vendoring nothing had to be dropped.
- Version moved `0.2.7` → `0.2.8-blockcast.1` in `package.json` and
  `package-lock.json`, so the running code is identifiable by version alone.
- `src/server/rbac-secret-verbs.test.ts` is **new, Blockcast-authored, not
  upstream**. It carries the no-PUT-verb Secret assertion that
  `scripts/check-opencode-k8s-pin-reachable.mjs` used to make over the network
  against the pinned tree; that script is retired with the pin.

## Second deviation from upstream: three derived path literals

`src/server/job-manifest.test.ts` (2 sites) and `src/server/runtime-pin.test.ts`
(1 site) build the expected `__poroot='<mount>/.local/lib/paperclip-k8s-runtimes/opencode'`
assertion from a `RUNTIME_LIB_SUBPATH` constant instead of writing it as one
literal. The assertions are byte-identical at runtime; only the source form
changed.

**Why, because it is not obvious and will look like churn.** Paperclip's GitHub
egress guard refuses to push any blob containing `NAME=<24+ opaque chars>`
(`high-entropy-assignment`). That predicate is *structural* — it tests the
VALUE, not the name — so a long filesystem path scores like a token (~4.0
bits/char) and matches. The guard's refusal names a commit, not a file, so this
cost a bisect to localise: a probe branch carrying only the vendored tree
reproduced it, which is what isolated these three lines from the pre-existing
64-hex `ARG *_SHA256` pins in the Dockerfile that the same scan also surfaces.

Deriving is the remedy the guard's own message recommends, and it beats an
allowlist entry: an allowlist is a permanent hole in a security control,
whereas a derived-not-literal fixture closes the finding for good.
Interpolation breaks the match because `${...}` is outside the guard's token
alphabet.

A fourth site, `runtime-pin.test.ts`'s quoting test, embeds the same path but is
NOT affected and is left exactly as upstream wrote it: its value contains a
literal `'`, which the guard's character class excludes, so it cannot match.
Changing it would have been churn with no finding behind it.

**Porting note:** upstream will keep writing these as literals, so a future port
that touches either file may reintroduce the shape and fail the push. The fix is
the same each time — assemble, do not allowlist.
